trace.title: Content flow
trace.detail:
## Understand the idea

Normal flow is the starting point: blocks stack and inline content flows within a line.

The box model adds padding and border around content. box-sizing:border-box makes a declared width include padding and border. It does not make every child shrink automatically.

Use Flexbox for one-dimensional distribution: a toolbar, row, or column. Use Grid when rows and columns should align together.

A flexible item may refuse to shrink below its min-content size. min-width:0 on the right child or minmax(0,1fr) on a grid track often fixes a long code/title overflow.

Find the actual owner before applying it everywhere.

Responsive design follows content constraints. A breakpoint is where this layout stops working, not a universal device category.

Use relative sizing, wrapping, and a readable line length. Keep DOM reading order sensible instead of using visual order to repair confusing markup.

trace.title: Follow one item
trace.detail:
Inspect the overflowing element's bounding box. Walk to its grid/flex parent.

Check min-size, fixed width, padding, and white-space. Change one rule, observe the effect, then remove temporary patches.

A 100vw child plus body padding can overflow. A fixed-height card can cut off translated text.

Avoid hiding overflow as the first repair because it can conceal controls or focused content.

trace.title: Try the failure
trace.detail: A layout can look correct with short English text and fail with a long title or 200% zoom. overflow:hidden can hide the symptom while clipping important content.
